opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running and repairing gas pipelines and the electric grid, restoring service after storms, and serving customers day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of pipelines, power plants and grid equipment over their long lives — a non-cash charge that rises as NiSource invests.

opex.name: Other taxes
opex.note: Mostly property and payroll-type taxes (trackers and riders moved some amounts this quarter, so it is lower than a year ago).

opex.name: Loss on sale of assets, net
opex.note: A small net loss on assets sold during the quarter.

footerNote: NiSource's short earnings release carries no income statement, so the figures come from its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q (filed the same day), rounded to the nearest $M. Net income is the $129.5M available to common shareholders: consolidated net income was $139.0M, of which $9.5M belonged to noncontrolling interests — that partner share is deducted below the line here (the equity line). Cost of energy (gas purchased for customers and fuel) is treated as the cost of revenue, as on our other utility pages.

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: Q3 is seasonally NiSource's softest quarter

oneTimers: The quarter's GAAP result needed almost no adjustments — adjusted net income was $130.9M versus $129.5M GAAP. The small gap is weather (about $4M unfavorable versus normal) and $6M of 'Value Captured' initiative costs, partly offset in the reconciliation.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of about $211M — the cost of funding a heavy construction program — partly offset by $22M of other income, for a net $188M cost below operating profit. A further $9.5M of profit belonged to noncontrolling-interest partners.

segments.name: Columbia Gas operations
segments.note: Gas distribution under the Columbia Gas brands — about 3.3M customers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Kentucky, Maryland and Indiana. Revenue up 4%; summer is the quiet season for heating gas.

segments.name: NIPSCO (Northern Indiana)
segments.note: Northern Indiana Public Service Co. — electricity for about 500,000 customers plus gas service in northern Indiana. Revenue up 6% on summer cooling demand and rate-base growth; electric is the bigger earner in Q3.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Mostly new data-center customer revenue and wholesale sales of excess capacity — up from just $1M a year ago as the data-center strategy starts to land.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter (SEC EDGAR) — income statement & segment detail

takeaways.text: Net income available to common shareholders rose to $129.5M ($0.27 a share) from $94.7M a year ago — a strong result for the summer quarter, which is seasonally NiSource's weakest because gas heating demand is low.
takeaways.title: A strong soft-season quarter

takeaways.text: NiSource extended its capital plan to 2033: $40B of spending ($32B base plan plus $8B for data centers), targeting 10–11% compound annual adjusted EPS growth for 2027–2033, with 2027 adjusted EPS guided to $2.22–$2.30.
takeaways.title: A bigger, longer build-out

takeaways.text: A new agreement with Microsoft expanded expected savings for existing customers from the GenCo data-center program to about $1.75B — big tech's power bills are being used to hold down everyone else's rates.
takeaways.title: Microsoft deal grows

verdict: Profit rose 37% to $130M in the seasonally soft summer quarter — and the real headline was a $40B seven-year build-out supercharged by data-center power deals, including a new Microsoft agreement.
